rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-marʿā means vegetation and green forage; the cited verse uses it for pasture growing from soil.
rows.anchor: والذي أخرج المرعى "  أي النبات والكلأ الأخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is vegetation, grass, and debris cast by floods onto valley sides; the form may also be intensified, and its plural is aghthāʾ.
rows.anchor: الغثاء : ما يقذف به السيل على جوانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات والقماش

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses ghuthāʾ as something dry; crushed, dried greens and useless debris around water are also called ghuthāʾ or hasheem.
rows.anchor: قتادة : الغثاء : الشيء اليابس .   ويقال للبقل والحشيش إذا تحطم ويبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term also describes water covered by useless foam and floating debris.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الماء : إذا علاه من الزبد والقماش ما لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā means black; vegetation can darken almost to black through intense greenness, since ḥawa means blackness.
rows.anchor: والأحوى : الأسود ، أي أن النبات يضرب إلى الحوة من شدة الخضرة كالأسود

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: The cited poem uses ḥawa for a slight dark-brown tint of the lips, a desirable shade.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى{[15971]} : لَمْيَاءُ في شَفَتَيْهَا

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines ḥawa as the brownness of a lip; aḥwā describes a man, ḥawwā a woman, and a camel may be green mixed with black.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح : والحوة : سمرة الشفة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā may be a circumstantial qualifier of al-marʿā, with the sense that God brought it out dark-green before making it debris.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " أحوى " حالا من " المرعى " ، ويكون المعنى : كأنه من خضرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ḥawā is an adjective of ghuthāʾ: the vegetation became debris after being green.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " حوى " صفة ل " غثاء " . والمعنى : أنه صار كذلك بعد خضرته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the plant becomes black from burning and age; fresh vegetation turns black when dry.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : فجعله أسود من احتراقه وقدمه ، والرطب إذا يبس أسود

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says God first brought out green pasture, then it dried, blackened, and became debris carried off by wind and floods.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : أخرج المرعى أخضر ، ثم لما يبس أسود من احتراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's loss of freshness is an image of unbelievers and the world's disappearance after its bloom.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل ضربه الله تعالى للكفار ، لذهاب الدنيا بعد نضارتها

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī cites ḥawiya al-nabāt and a line about dark, rain-grown valleys as evidence for the verb describing vegetation turning dark.
rows.anchor: قد حوي النبت ؛ حكاه الكسائي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the exception to mean that God will not will the Prophet to forget anything, comparing the construction with the exception in Hūd 11:108.
rows.anchor: ما قاله الفراء : إلا ما شاء الله ، وهو لم يشأ أن تنسى شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom I will give you everything you ask except what you wish can express an intention to withhold nothing.
rows.anchor: ويقال في الكلام : لأعطينك كل ما سألت إلا ما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this construction, oath exceptions follow the swearer's intention of completing the oath rather than withholding anything.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا مجاري الإيمان ، يستثنى فيها ونية الحالف التمام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet did not forget anything after this verse was revealed until he died.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح عن ابن عباس : فلم ينس بعد نزول هذه الآية حتى مات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Saʿīd reports Qatāda's statement that the Messenger of God forgot nothing, except as the verse qualifies.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة ، قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation allows that God could will the Prophet to forget, while affirming that he forgot none of the revelation after this verse descended.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال قيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، ولكنه لم ينسى شيئا منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view allows temporary forgetting followed by recollection, so the Prophet could forget without losing the passage permanently.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، ثم يذكر بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says the Prophet omitted a verse during prayer; Ubay thought it had been abrogated, but the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة ، فحسب أبي أنها نسخت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some understand forgetting as abrogation, distinguishing the abrogation of recitation from leaving practice after its ruling is abrogated.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل : هذا بمعنى النسخ ، أي إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه . والاستثناء نوع من النسخ

rows.speaker: الفرغاني
rows.claim: Al-Farghānī recounts that Ibn Kaysān answered Junayd's question by glossing do not forget as do not fail to act on the revelation; Ibn Kaysān praised the answer.
rows.anchor: قال الفرغاني : كان يغشى مجلس الجنيد أهل البسط من العلوم ، وكان يغشاه ابن كيسان النحوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tansā is read as negation rather than prohibition; the prohibition reading takes it as a command not to neglect recitation, with forgetting possible if recitation is removed.
rows.anchor: للنفي لا للنهي . وقيل : للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers negation: an exception from a prohibition is ordinarily bounded by a known time, and the yāʾ is written in every codex and read by the reciters.
rows.anchor: والأول هو المختار ؛ لأن الاستثناء من النهي لا يكاد يكون إلا مؤقتا معلوما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation reads the exception as God's willing to delay the revelation's descent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view connects the exception to the pasture becoming dry debris: what people and animals benefit from is spared that fate.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى فجعله غثاء أحوى إلا ما شاء الله أن ينال بنو آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jahr is what is expressed openly in speech and deeds, while what is hidden is secret.
rows.anchor: أي الإعلان من القول والعمل . " وما يخفى " من السر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what is hidden as what lies in one's heart and self.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ما في قلبك ونفسك

rows.speaker: محمد بن حاتم
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim takes the contrast as publicizing charity versus concealing it.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن حاتم : يعلم إعلان الصدقة وإخفاءها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes what is public the Quran memorized in the Prophet's chest and what is hidden the recitation abrogated from it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجهر ما حفظته من القرآن في صدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-nuyassiruka coordinates with sa-nuqriʾuka, while the statement that God knows the manifest and hidden is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: معطوف على " سنقرئك " وقوله : " إنه يعلم الجهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusrā is the easier way, namely doing good works.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " لليسرى " أي للطريقة اليسرى ، وهي عمل الخير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the promise as enabling the Prophet to do good.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نيسرك لأن تعمل خيرا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies al-yusrā as Paradise.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود : " لليسرى " أي للجنة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God guides the Prophet to the easy, tolerant Ḥanīfī law.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نوفقك للشريعة اليسرى ، وهي الحنيفية السمحة السهلة . قال معناه الضحاك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God makes revelation easy for the Prophet to memorize and act upon.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي نهون عليك الوحي حتى تحفظه وتعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command tells Muḥammad to admonish his people with the Quran.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " فذكر " أي فعظ قومك يا محمد بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikrā means admonition or reminder.
rows.anchor: " إن نفعت الذكرى " أي الموعظة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the reminder is an admonition for believers and a proof against unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وروى يونس عن الحسن قال : تذكرة للمؤمن ، وحجة على الكافر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the reminder benefits God's allies but not His enemies.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول : تنفع أوليائي ، ولا تنفع أعدائي

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjānī holds that reminding is obligatory even when it does not benefit; the condition means whether or not it benefits, with ellipsis as in al-Naḥl 16:81.
rows.anchor: وقال الجرجاني : التذكير واجب وإن لم ينفع . والمعنى : فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view restricts the verse to particular people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه مخصوص بأقوام بأعيانهم

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara takes in as meaning mā, so the command is to remind whenever reminder benefits; the reminder is beneficial in every case.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن " إن " بمعنى ما ، أي فذكر ما نفعت الذكرى ، فتكون " إن " بمعنى ما

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: Some grammarians take in as idh, meaning when, as in Āl ʿImrān 3:139, where ascendancy is stated in the condition of faith.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العربية : " أن " " إن " بمعنى إذ ، أي إذ نفعت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further grammatical opinion says in means qad.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بمعنى قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who fears is someone mindful of and afraid of God.
rows.anchor: أي من يتقي الله ويخافه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that this verse was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: فروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī says a hopeful person may also remember, but reminder affects the fearful more strongly, so the verse names fear even though both fear and hope are involved.
rows.anchor: الماوردي : وقد يذكر من يرجوه ، إلا أن تذكرة الخاشي أبلغ من تذكرة الراجي

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the Prophet should admonish everyone; even if only the fearful benefit, he earns the reward of calling people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي عمم أنت التذكير والوعظ ، وإن كان الوعظ إنما ينفع من يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched person avoids the reminder and keeps away from it.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ويتجنبها " أي ويتجنب الذكرى ويبعد عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashqā is the one known in God's knowledge to be wretched.
rows.anchor: " الأشقى " أي الشقي في علم الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported occasion identifies the verse's subject as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وعتبة بن ربيعة

words: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will not die and thereby find relief from torment, nor will he live a life that benefits him.
rows.anchor: " ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى " أي لا يموت فيستريح من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line uses the same paradox for a soul that neither dies to end its suffering nor lives a life with any taste.
rows.anchor: ألا ما لنفسٍ لا تموتُ فينقضي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Muslim transmits from Abū Saʿīd that monotheist believers who enter Hell, described by al-Farrāʾ as the lesser fire, burn and die there until intercession is made for them.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي سعيد الخدري ، وأن الموحدين من المؤمنين إذا دخلوا جهنم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the wretched differ in degree: this severe threat concerns the most wretched, while others do not reach that rank.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أهل الشقاء متفاوتون في شقائهم ، هذا الوعيد للأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read in the second person, tuthirūn; Ubay's reading adds antum and confirms that address.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة " بل تؤثرون " بالتاء ، تصديقه قراءة أُبيّ " بل أنتم تؤثرون "

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read yuʾthirūn in the third person, with the most wretched understood as the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم " بل يؤثرون " بالياء على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second-person reading, the address is to Muslims who prefer accumulating worldly life in order to accumulate reward.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأول فيكون تأويلها بل تؤثرون أيها المسلمون الاستكثار من الدنيا ، للاستكثار من الثواب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains that people choose the present world's ready food, drink, pleasures, and beauty, while the afterlife is unseen; they take the immediate and leave the deferred.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ هذه الآية ، فقال : أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ؟

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Anas reports that Abū Mūsā urged him to remember God when travelers dwelt on worldly matters; Abū Mūsā said the world hastens while the afterlife is hidden, and seeing it would leave no one wavering or preferring this life.
rows.anchor: وروى ثابت عن أنس قال : كنا مع أبي موسى في مسير ، والناس يتكلمون ويذكرون الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira refers here to the abode of the afterlife, namely Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي والدار الآخرة ، أي الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better, meaning superior, and more lasting than the present world.
rows.anchor: " خير " أي أفضل . " وأبقى " أي أدوم من الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the world in relation to the afterlife to a finger dipped in the sea, and asks what it brings back; al-Qurṭubī labels the report sound.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كما يضع أحدكم أصبعه في اليم

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār argues that even if the world were perishing gold and the afterlife enduring pottery, one should choose the latter; in fact the afterlife is enduring gold and this world perishing pottery.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار : لو كانت الدنيا من ذهب يفنى

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take this to mean the teaching that the afterlife is better and more lasting; God's books repeatedly affirm it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وابن زيد : يريد قوله " والآخرة خير وأبقى " .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan understands the earlier scriptures to mean all the books of God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " قال : كتب الله جل ثناؤه كلها

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says this refers to the passage from qad aflaḥa through the end of the sūra, citing the forthcoming Abū Dharr report.
rows.anchor: الكلبي : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " من قوله : " قد أفلح " إلى آخر السورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that this means the whole sūra.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " قال : هذه السورة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes this to mean that the Quran is present in earlier books.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : إن هذا القرآن لفي الصحف الأولى ، أي الكتب الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are the books revealed to Abraham and Moses; the exact wording need not occur there, since the same meaning is intended.
rows.anchor: يعني الكتب المنزلة عليهما . ولم يرد أن هذه الألفاظ بعينها في تلك الصحف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In al-Ājurrī's report from Abū Dharr, Abraham's scrolls tell a powerful, tested, deluded ruler to defend the oppressed rather than amass wealth; God answers even an unbeliever's plea when oppressed.
rows.anchor: فما كانت صحف إبراهيم ؟ قال : كانت أمثالا كلها : أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلى المغرور

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The scrolls say a wise person should set aside an hour for communion with God, an hour for self-accounting and reflection on God's favor, and an hour for personal needs such as food and drink.
rows.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون له ثلاث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: They say one should travel only to prepare for the return, maintain one's livelihood, or seek a lawful pleasure, and should understand one's time, attend to one's affairs, and guard one's tongue.
rows.anchor: وعلى العاقل ألا يكون ظاعنا إلا في ثلاث : تزود لمعاد ، ومرمة لمعاش

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: They say that whoever counts speech among deeds speaks little except about what concerns him.
rows.anchor: ومن عد كلامه من عمله قل كلامه إلا فيما يعينه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Moses's scrolls wonder that someone certain of death rejoices, someone certain of destiny exhausts himself, or someone who sees the world's reversals feels secure in it.
rows.anchor: قال : كانت عبرا كلها : عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت كيف يفرح ! وعجبت لمن أيقن بالقدر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: They also wonder that someone certain of tomorrow's reckoning fails to act.
rows.anchor: وعجبت لمن أيقن بالحساب غدا ثم هو لا يعمل !

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked whether anything from those scrolls remains in what God revealed to the Prophet, he answers yes and recites this sūra's verses on purification, prayer, preferring this world, and the enduring afterlife.
rows.anchor: فهل في أيدينا شيء مما كان في يديه إبراهيم وموسى ، مما أنزل الله عليك ؟ قال : نعم اقرأ يا أبا ذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad is commanded to admonish and warn them.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " فذكر " أي فعظهم يا محمد وخوفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is only an admonisher.
rows.anchor: " إنما أنت مذكر " أي واعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to dominate them or kill them; the author says the sword verse later abrogated this ruling.
rows.anchor: " لست عليهم بمصيطر " أي بمسلط عليهم فتقتلهم . ثم نسختها آية السيف

rows.speaker: هارون الأعور
rows.claim: Hārūn al-Aʿwar reads the word with fatḥa on ṭāʾ, as in al-musayṭarūn in al-Ṭūr 52:37; the form is Tamīm dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هارون الأعور " بمسيطَر " ( بفتح الطاء )

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines musayṭir as one who controls something, oversees and tends its affairs, and records its deeds.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح : " المسيطر والمصيطر : المسلط على الشيء ، ليشرف عليه ، ويتعهد أحواله

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ derives the word from sṭr, since writing stays within a line; the text also gives the idiom sayṭarta ʿalaynā.
rows.anchor: من معنى السطر ألا يتجاوز ، فالكتاب مسطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb saṭarahu can also mean to knock someone down.
rows.anchor: وسطره أي صرعه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Muqātil report that Hell is dragged by seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels, and roars until set to the left of the Throne; Muslim transmits Ibn Masʿūd's report of the reins and angels from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود ومقاتل : تقاد جهنم بسبعين ألف زمام ، كل زمام بيد سبعين ألف ملك

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet's color changed and his companions noticed; he said Gabriel had recited the preceding verse and this one to him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري : لما نزلت " وجيء يومئذ بجهنم " تغير لون رسول الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In ʿAlī's report, Hell is led by the seventy thousand reins and would burn the gathered people if it broke free; presented to Muḥammad, it says God has forbidden his flesh to it, and everyone cries for themselves except Muḥammad, who pleads for his community.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه : قلت يا رسول الله ، كيف يجاء بها ؟ قال : ( تؤتى بها تقاد بسبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the person recollects in the sense of taking heed and repenting; the person is an unbeliever or someone whose chief concern was worldly life.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان " أي يتعظ ويتوب . وهو الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person has no opportunity for admonition and repentance then, having neglected them in worldly life.
rows.anchor: " وأنى له الذكرى " أي ومن أين له الاتعاظ والتوبة وقد فرط فيها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also glosses it as asking how recollection could benefit; an omitted genitive must be supplied, otherwise recollection on that day conflicts with the claim that it is unavailable.
rows.anchor: بين " يومئذ يتذكر " وبين " وأنى له الذكرى " تناف . قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and others say the two elevated routes are the paths of good and evil, made clear through the messengers God sent.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود وغيرهما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports a Prophetic saying that there are two routes, good and evil, and God did not make the evil route dearer to people than the good one.
rows.anchor: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the two rises are the two breasts; this is also attributed to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAlī, since they are routes to an infant's life and provision.
rows.anchor: النجدان : الثديان . وهو قول سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najd means elevation and its plural is nujūd; the region Najd is so called because it rises above low-lying Tihāma.
rows.anchor: فالنجد : العلو ، وجمعه نجود

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: The cited line uses najd for the elevated route across Najd Kabkab.
rows.anchor:
قال امرؤ القيس :
فريقان منهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One parsing takes mā as a verbal noun, so the phrase means the soul and its fashioning.
rows.anchor: قيل : المعنى وتسويتها . " فما " : بمعنى المصدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing takes mā as meaning who, referring to God as the one who fashioned the soul.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ومن سواها ، وهو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The soul may refer either to Adam or to every human soul.
rows.anchor: وفي النفس قولان : أحدهما آدم . الثاني : كل نفس منفوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwā means prepared or made ready.
rows.anchor: وسوى : بمعنى هيأ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as fashioning and proportioning the soul's creation.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : سواها : سوى خلقها وعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these nouns are genitive as objects of the oath.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأسماء كلها مجرورة على القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by His creation because its wondrous workmanship points to Him.
rows.anchor: أقسم جل ثناؤه بخلقه لما فيه من عجائب الصنعة الدالة عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, in Ibn Abī Najīḥ's report, glosses alhamahā as made it know the paths of wickedness and piety; Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same explanation.
rows.anchor: أي عرفها طريق الفجور والتقوى ، وقاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also explains the two terms as obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا : عرفها الطاعة والمعصية

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says that when God wills good for a servant He inspires good and the servant acts on it; when He wills harm, He inspires evil and the servant acts on it.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب قال : إذا أراد الله عز وجل بعبده خيرا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God made the soul know the paths of good and evil, as in the two paths of al-Balad 90:10.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : " فألهمها " قال : عرفها طريق الخير وطريق الشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying that God inspires the pious believer with piety and the profligate with his wickedness.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : ألهم المؤمن المتقي تقواه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God made the soul's wickedness and piety clear to it.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة قال : بين لها فجورها وتقواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding explanations have approximately the same meaning.
rows.anchor: والمعنى متقارب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited the verse and prayed for God to grant his soul piety and purify it, since God is the best purifier and its guardian and master.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة قال : قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Juwaybir reports through al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet raised his voice while reciting the verse and prayed for his soul's piety, saying God is its guardian and best purifier.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fujūr and al-taqwā are verbal nouns functioning as direct objects.
rows.anchor: والفجور والتقوى : مصدران في موضع المفعول به

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: In Muslim's report from Abū al-Aswad, ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn recounts debate over whether people's deeds are predetermined; after questioning the justice of that, Abū al-Aswad says God is not questioned, and ʿImrān explains he was testing him. Two men from Muzayna ask the Prophet the same, and he says their deeds were decreed, citing these verses as proof.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم ، عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي قال : قال لي عمران بن حصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the answer to the oath, with the sense لقد أفلح.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم ، بمعنى : لقد أفلح

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the lām was omitted because the discourse is long enough to substitute for it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : اللام حذفت ، لأن الكلام طال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the oath's response is omitted, with the implied sense that the hearers will surely be resurrected.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجواب محذوف ، أي والشمس وكذا وكذا لتبعثن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the missing oath response to mean God will destroy the Meccans for denying the Messenger, as He destroyed Thamūd for denying Ṣāliḥ; he treats this clause as an aside following the inspiration clause.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري : تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the successful one purifying the soul is an aside to God's inspiring it with wickedness and piety, not the oath's answer.
rows.anchor: على سبيل الاستطراد ، وليس من جواب القسم في شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view uses fronting and postponement without ellipsis: the successful and failed souls are stated before the sun and its brightness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو على التقديم والتأخير بغير حذف . والمعنى : قد أفلح من زكاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflaḥa means to succeed or attain felicity.
rows.anchor: أفلح " فاز . " من زكاها " أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful person is one whom God has purified through obedience.
rows.anchor: " من زكاها " أي من زكى الله نفسه بالطاعة
